_readme: ModOrder masterlist: what is known about D2RMM mods, so ModOrder.js can sort a mod list and warn about it (like LOOT's masterlist). One entry per mod. ids = D2RMM folder names it goes by (first = usual); names = mod.json names that identify a renamed folder. checked = the version the rules were written against. group = whole-file | top | early | default | late | patch | final (a mod never sorts above a lower group; whole-file mods copy entire tables, so they go first and every other mod, conversions included, patches their copy). after/before = {mod|tag, why, if}: when both are ticked. requires = {mod|plugin, min, why, if, level}: plugin = the DLL name without .dll as D2RMM imports it into d2rloader\. incompatible = {mod, why}. messages = {level: error|warn|info, text, if}. if = {ticked:[ids], notTicked:[ids], config:{key:value}} (all must hold). tags: 'conversion' (a data mod converted by the toolkit), 'skill-pages' (adds SkillTab4 pages), 'stock-lookup' (looks up plain-game rows by name: goes above the conversions, which rename or replace them). Players add their own rules in <D2RMM>\modorder-userlist.json (same format; its entries are merged over these).

Options that would replace another mod's work are left out and named in the install log. 0.3.0: renamed or moved skills are found (option Renamed skills for the ones it cannot find). 0.4.0: every choice is a trade inside the skill; a skill another mod changed, reworked or replaced gets alternative trades made from its own columns (option, on). 0.5.0: 113 stock skills (the Warlock's included), up to four choices; stops at 255 skills per class (option). 0.5.1: that option has 2047 for use with the Skill Limits plugin 0.2.0, which reads saves of a class with more than 255 skills.
